channel.title: GetDiscoverable.io — Notes on being found
channel.description: Plain-English writing on SEO, AEO, and GEO — how a business gets found by search engines and AI assistants. By Zillah Bahar.

item.title: Five Things Wineries Think Help Them Get Found by AI (That Don't)
item.description: Keyword stuffing, self-praise, PDF tasting sheets, social media, one-time SEO — five moves that feel like progress but don't get a winery named by AI. And what actually does.

item.title: How Do You Know If AI Is Recommending You? A Way to Actually Measure It
item.description: Most of your AI visibility is invisible in analytics. How to measure whether an assistant recommends you — ask the machines, track referrals, watch Search Console — and why "am I named?" beats any traffic number.

item.title: Will AI-Written Content Get Your Site Penalized? Here's What Actually Happens
item.description: Businesses fear Google will bury them for using AI to write. From Google's own policy: it doesn't penalize content for being AI — it penalizes thin, spammy content made to manipulate rankings, however it's produced.

item.title: Why AI Trusts Vivino and Wine-Searcher More Than Your Own Website
item.description: When an AI recommends a wine, it doesn't take your word for it — it checks what independent sources say about you. Why third-party reputation beats self-praise, and how to build a footprint a machine will believe.

item.title: Structured Data, Explained: The Hidden Labels That Get a Page Quoted by AI
item.description: What structured data actually is, walked field by field through a real page's schema — and why it's the piece that most directly decides whether an AI can quote you by name. COLAClear is the worked example.

item.title: Wineries' Biggest Fear Is Selling. So Why Is All Their AI Pointed at the Cellar?
item.description: InnoVint surveyed 541 wineries: demand is the industry's #1 worry, and 60% already use AI — almost all of it aimed inward, at making the wine. The opening is to point some of it outward, toward the AI buyers now shop with.

item.title: Harvard's Wine-and-AI Symposium Covered Everything — Except How Buyers Will Find You
item.description: The best minds in wine and data science spent three days on how AI will change winemaking. The fastest-changing question — whether an AI assistant can find and recommend your winery — barely came up.

item.title: Write for the Shopper and the Machine: The Two Layers Every Product Page Needs
item.description: Shoppers ask AI by occasion, budget, and pairing — never "minerality." But the machine still needs the facts to match you. How to write a product page for both readers at once.

item.title: The Distillery Website Checklist for Getting Found by AI
item.description: When a buyer asks an assistant to recommend a bourbon or gin, some distilleries get named and others vanish. Six fixable checks — in plain English — to make your distillery the one AI names.

item.title: How to Write a Spirits Tasting Note an AI Will Quote
item.description: Category, proof, mash bill, cask — the concrete facts that make a whiskey or gin tasting note quotable by AI, with a before-and-after that keeps your voice.

item.title: How to Write a Tasting Note an AI Will Actually Quote
item.description: Most tasting notes are written to sound beautiful. To get your wine recommended by AI, they need to be written to be read by a machine. The difference, with a before-and-after.

item.title: The Winery Website Checklist for Getting Found by AI
item.description: When a buyer asks an assistant to recommend a wine, some wineries get named and others vanish. Six fixable checks — in plain English — to make your winery the one AI names.

item.title: I Built This Site to Be Found by AI. Here's Exactly What I Did.
item.description: A transparent, plain-English teardown of everything I did to make this site discoverable by search engines and AI — every move, why it matters to a machine, and the honest timeline.

item.title: How Do Regulated Brands Get Found by AI?
item.description: The compliance habits that keep you legal — age walls, hedged copy, facts buried in PDFs — are often what makes you invisible to AI. How to fix it without crossing a line.

item.title: How Do I Make My Business Discoverable on AI?
item.description: The plain-English answer — six fixable steps to become the brand an AI assistant names when a buyer asks, no ad budget required.

item.title: How to Tell If AI Can't See Your Brand
item.description: When a buyer asks ChatGPT to recommend something in your category, does your brand come up? A seven-point self-check you can run in ten minutes — and the fix for each.

item.title: SEO vs AEO vs GEO: What's the Difference?
item.description: A plain-English guide to the three ways people and AI find you online in 2026 — search engines, answer engines, and generative engines — and why you can no longer optimize for only the first.

item.title: How I Got COLAClear Cited by Name in Google's AI Overview
item.description: A first-person account of the work behind a by-name AI citation — writing for real questions, machine-readable signals (schema.org, llms.txt), AI-crawler access, and earned authority. No budget, no team.

item.title: Why AI Recommends Some Wineries by Name — and Never Mentions Yours
item.description: When a buyer asks ChatGPT for a great bottle, some wineries get named and others vanish. What separates them — machine-readable text, one consistent name, structured data, open crawler access — and how to fix it.
